package application

import (
	"context"

	iamdomain "metaldocs/internal/modules/iam/domain"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (suppression, STRING LITERAL): the directive's
// characters appearing in data must not act as a directive.
//
// A suppression implemented by scanning the raw source line cannot tell code
// from data. Under that implementation the string below — an error message, a
// doc snippet, a log line, anything that happens to quote the guard's own
// vocabulary — silences the rule on the very line that violates it. Worse, it
// does so invisibly: nothing in the file looks like an opt-out.
//
// Reading the parsed comments instead makes the distinction structural. The
// scanner already knows which bytes are a comment and which are a literal, so
// the analyzer does not have to guess, and a suppression can only be written
// where a human reviewer would recognize one.
//
// This file must still be reported.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func chargeStringSuppressed(ctx context.Context) string {
	return iamdomain.UserIDFromContext(ctx) + "//cilint:allow-actor-extraction pretend rationale"
}
